title: Imports and reusable prompts
qualification: Imported paths and captured source closures follow the declaring source and selected host.
benefit: Share project conventions once and reuse them across agent files.
example: A shared review checklist imported by several project assistants.

title: Built-in tools
qualification: ChatMD read_dir and model-visible read_directory are distinct names; declarations do not grant all host authority.
benefit: Give an agent practical abilities without writing each tool yourself.
example: Read project files, propose edits, or ingest a supplied web page.

title: MCP tools and authentication
qualification: Maintained outbound MCP tools and OAuth are separate from deprecated prompt serving and daemon authentication.
benefit: Connect an agent to capabilities exposed by an MCP server.
example: Bring an existing authenticated tool service into your workflow.

title: Custom OCaml tools
qualification: Progress and traces are transient and need their own disclosure policy; the tracked example has companion Dune dependencies.
benefit: Expose an application-specific operation as a typed tool.
example: Wrap a domain calculation or service call in an OCaml implementation.

title: Retrieval and indexing
qualification: Agent retrieval uses configured embeddings; test vectors are not semantic retrieval and website search uses a separate index.
benefit: Find relevant passages without pasting an entire documentation set.
example: A research assistant retrieves project notes before drafting an answer.

title: Prompt refinement and evaluation
qualification: Local template and paid online strategies differ; append behavior and model costs matter. The broad older library overview needs reconciliation.
benefit: Iterate on an agent’s instructions with an explicit evaluation process.
example: Compare a revised review prompt against a defined set of tasks.

title: Compaction and retained history
qualification: Summaries are lossy; visible history, canonical history, exports, and archived states are distinct representations.
benefit: Manage the context of a conversation as the work grows.
example: Retain a working summary while keeping history representations distinct.

title: Programmable ChatML workflows
qualification: Capabilities depend on the host. Turn, event-drain, and job limits are not dollar caps; detailed phase contracts retain their historical scope.
benefit: Put workflow decisions in a script when instructions alone are insufficient.
example: Collect check results, assign failed cases to specialists, and report the evidence.

title: Jobs, timers, and restart
qualification: Recovery does not resume arbitrary continuations or guarantee exactly-once external effects.
benefit: Let a host manage work after a client disconnects.
example: Dispatch a specialist job and handle its completion in a moderator.

title: Terminal controls and drafts
qualification: Attachments, exports, keybindings, and optional draft suggestions follow host-specific behavior; suggestions may send unsent text and incur costs.
benefit: Inspect and steer an agent from a local terminal.
example: Review tool activity while working in the project’s own directory.

title: Custom shell capabilities and guardrails
qualification: Legacy Session_store commands do not administer daemon IDs; a declaration alone does not authorize execution.
benefit: Design useful shell tools with reusable runtimes and project-specific review rules.
example: Give inspection and build commands different access, with ChatML or an agent reviewing selected requests.

title: Persistent and generated specialists
qualification: Persistent children require an admitted durable host; generated children select existing inherited tools and retain their restrictions.
benefit: Delegate focused work while keeping useful specialist conversations available for follow-up.
example: Create a reviewer for a failing tutorial, retain its session, and send updated evidence.

title: Reusable and stateful script tools
qualification: Standalone tools have fresh invocation globals. Stateful tools require a supported moderator handler and explicit invocation resolution.
benefit: Extend agent behavior with ChatML logic and selected existing capabilities.
example: Expose a report calculator as a standalone tool or retain a queue of reviews in moderator state.

title: Clients and synchronization
qualification: Protocol 1.0 synchronization does not promise replay of live deltas; reconnect restores authoritative projections.
benefit: Build a client that connects to a running agent.
example: Use stdio or HTTP to send requests and inspect authoritative session state.

title: OCaml integration and older APIs
qualification: Current actor-owned hosts and older file-backed session APIs have different storage and lifetime owners.
benefit: Integrate Ochat’s current host interfaces into an OCaml application.
example: Build an application around an actor-owned agent session.

title: Commands and utilities
qualification: Installed names, utility subcommands, and source-only demos are distinguished explicitly.
benefit: Use Ochat from scripts as well as interactive conversations.
example: Save a project report from a single batch invocation.
